messages:
Jane (customer): Hey team — our web app's streaming responses are flaking for a subset of Safari users. They get a chunk or two, then the connection closes. In the console we see repeated token refreshes and occasional 304 responses from the CDN. Impacting prod traffic, some customers see full disconnect loops.

Maya (Support): Sorry about that, Jane — can you paste a minimal HAR or curl that reproduces? Do you know if they’re on iOS or macOS Safari? Any repro steps you can share?

Jane (customer): Mostly macOS Safari 16.4, also a few iPhones on 16.x. Quick repro: open page, start the SSE-based chat, after ~20-40s stream stops. If they wait it sometimes reconnects but then immediately asks the frontend to refresh tokens and fails with 401 from /auth/refresh.

Maya (Support): Thanks. @Eric / @Ryan can you triage? This smells like an EventSource vs CDN cache edge case we’ve seen before, but the 304+auth churn is odd.

Eric (Eng - runtime): On it. A few notes: browsers differ in how they handle EventSource + Authorization headers (EventSource cannot set headers), so some customers put tokens in the URL, which makes responses cacheable unless we set proper cache headers / vary. Safari has known quirks where if the connection is treated as cached or gets an intermediary 304, it may close or not flush partial chunks.

Ryan (Frontend): We do use the polyfill for older Safari: https://github.com/Yaffle/EventSource or a XHR-stream-based fallback. That polyfill opens an XHR and streams chunks; if the edge returns 304 on revalidate requests, the XHR polyfill sometimes interprets that as EOF and immediately tears down, then client code tries to refresh token and reopen. Could be an auth race if refresh endpoint is rate limited.

Lina (Infra): Can you share the edge logs? Also which CDN (Cloudflare/Cloudfront)? We recently enabled s3 origin revalidate TTL for that path. If the CDN revalidates and returns 304, the connection semantics for long-lived streams get weird.

Jane (customer): Using Cloudflare. I can get you a HAR and a failing user agent string.

Maya (Support): Please include HAR + network tab. Meanwhile Eric, any quick mitigation for Jane to unblock?

Eric (Eng - runtime): Short-term mitigation: ensure the streaming endpoint responses include headers that prevent revalidation for EventSource paths. Example headers we recommend: "Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate" and "Vary: Authorization" AND set "Connection: keep-alive". For Cloudflare, set a Page Rule to bypass cache for /v1/streams* or add a Cache-Control origin header with s-maxage=0 and no-transform. Also avoid putting tokens in query params if possible — prefer cookie-based session proxied through our API gateway.

Ryan (Frontend): Another workaround on the client: polyfill users — add a reconnection backoff and a guard that prevents immediate token refresh/reauth loops. For example: if XHR polyfill gets 304 or 0-length chunk, wait 5s before trying refresh; keep a counter so we don't hit the refresh endpoint repeatedly.

Jane (customer): I can flip a Cloudflare rule to bypass cache for the stream path now. Will that stop the 304s?

Lina (Infra): Bypassing cache should stop revalidation 304 responses. Also add response header "Vary: Authorization" so caches won't serve the same cached body to different tokens. If you can't change client usage of token-in-url immediately, at least set cache bypass for that route.

Eric (Eng - runtime): We're also seeing in our logs that when the connection is torn down by the edge returning 304 mid-stream, the runtime sometimes emits a partial chunk and then Mark as closed which Safari interprets as EOF instead of keep-alive — causing clients to attempt immediate reconnects. We'll push a soft change that ensures the runtime flushes a final sentinel event (e.g., :keepalive) before treat-as-closed when a revalidate comes through, but that's more of a band-aid.

Ryan (Frontend): Sharing a repro curl for ops to run (streaming test):

```
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?session_token=REDACTED"
```

If you see HTTP/1.1 304 in the middle of chunks, you've hit the revalidation issue.

Maya (Support): Noted. Jane, if you can toggle the Cloudflare Page Rule now and confirm, we'll monitor. Also please collect a console log of the polyfill's XHR responses (status codes + responseText length) — that helps us confirm the polyfill misinterpreting 304 as EOF.

Jane (customer): Toggled bypass for /v1/streams*, rolling out now. Will update in ~10m.

[~8 minutes later]

Jane (customer): After bypassing cache, the stream is stable for one of the previously failing users. Still seeing one user with disconnects but no 304s in the logs — looks like real Safari bug.

Eric (Eng - runtime): OK progress. For the remaining user, ask them to disable any browser extensions and check whether they are behind a proxy that might transform responses (gzip vs chunked). Safari can be sensitive to Transfer-Encoding: chunked + gzip interplay. If the proxy unzips/re-zips, it can break streaming semantics.

Ryan (Frontend): We should add a protective heuristic in the polyfill: treat 304 as a transient error (retry after jitter) instead of EOF. I'll open a small frontend PR to add that backoff and a max-refresh-per-minute throttle so token refresh can't be hammered.

Lina (Infra): On the infra side, we should make the stream route explicitly uncacheable at the CDN layer and ensure our edge config doesn't do conditional requests (no If-Modified-Since / If-None-Match) for open SSE connections. I'll file a change and tag @deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: Rolling change ticket INF-2412 created and queued for canary. Will deploy to edge cluster 3 in 10 minutes.

Eric (Eng - runtime): Followups we need to do: 1) Runtime: emit an explicit streaming keepalive frame on stream close events so clients get a last flush. 2) Frontend: polyfill backoff + token refresh throttle. 3) Infra: CDN page rule to bypass /v1/streams and set Cache-Control + Vary. 4) Support: monitor support tickets for same UA.

Maya (Support): Thanks everyone. Jane — can you keep this thread updated if you see any residuals after infra canary goes live? We'll keep the ticket open until fully resolved.

Jane (customer): Will do. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:

Eric (Eng - runtime): One more note for debugging: if you can get the user's network capture and grep for any repeated requests to /auth/refresh within seconds of each other, that indicates the token refresh loop. That often comes from polyfills that immediately reconnect on short disconnects. Throttle that refresh to reduce downstream billing/rate-limit impact.

Ryan (Frontend): I'll land the polyfill PR with a default 3s jitter + exponential backoff and a threshold of 3 refresh attempts per minute.

Lina (Infra): Canary started on edge cluster 3 — patch to bypass cache for /v1/streams pushed. Monitor dashboards for 5m.

[~5 minutes later]

Lina (Infra): Canary looks good — no 304s for test sessions. Rolling to remaining clusters.

Jane (customer): After full rollout, the affected users are stable. No more 304s and much fewer disconnects. Thanks!

Maya (Support): Marking resolved for now. We'll keep INF-2412 open for the runtime keepalive sentinel work and the frontend polyfill PR.

Eric (Eng - runtime): Filed RUNTIME-689 to add final sentinel event on mid-stream revalidate.

Ryan (Frontend): PR: https://git.redwood.internal/r/redwood/frontend/pulls/1421 — adds polyfill backoff + refresh throttle.

Maya (Support): Closing the support ticket; reopen if anything reappears. :thumbsup:
